# Chapter Twelve: Check and Mate

Marcus awoke with a start “Maelen” he breathed trying to sit up as gentle hands held him down. “Don’t move, you’re still healing” came a familiar woman’s voice and opening his eyes he found the smiling face of Dara hovering over him. Her green eyes sparkled as she smiled down at him his head felt like a ton and everything hurt, but he was alive his mind went back remembering the fight, the mage “Maelen” he croaked, and Dara’s smile fell. He sacrificed himself to save us” she whispered laying a gentle hand on Marcus’s chest. He laid back as tears welled up in his eyes first Orah and now Maelen he was losing what few friends he had fast “He thought about the Seer about his power, the runes and what he had seen, it had been incredible the amount of power he had wielded Marcus thought blinking back the tears as Dara sat there silently watching him.

“How am I” he asked moving his limbs and trying to get a feel for if he was in one piece or not, the Seer had done a number on him before Maelen had stepped in he thought morosely. “You still have a week of recovery Marcus” came another familiar voice as he looked over to see Patrice entering the room, she looked haggard and from the blood shot eyes he had guessed crying. “Im so sorry Patrice” Marcus said, and the woman looked down nodding. “He saved us” she said, the simple statement an affirmation of his bravery and greatness as Patrice walked over to a wooden cabinet and began pulling out supplies and placing them on a tray.

“We need to change the bandages, but you have been out for nearly a week and a half, between myself and the Silvan healers we have been able to bring you to nearly healed in a fraction of the time. “They have technologies and even some magic that is well beyond our own” she answered, and he could hear the appreciation of there craft even beyond the undertone of hurt that still rang in her words. “Once you are well there is a General Durass who wishes to speak to you” Dara said still sitting on the edge of the small bed. “Where are we?” Marcus asked realizing the room was not familiar to him, it was ornate, and he spied carved animals climbing the walls, the architecture was dark and warm as ornate wood bannisters and railings surrounded the room.

“We are in the Barrens, the Sylvan’s took us in, once we explained who we were, they brought us to the city and set us in this room, though we are not to have contact with anyone as of yet” she said and he could hear the worry in her voice. What had happened he wondered.

It was a day later, still wrapped in bandages as Marcus was finally able to get out of bed, hobbling down the hall he caught his first glimpse of the outside as his breath caught in his throat. He looked out over the giant trees as the terraces and platforms covered with buildings. “It’s a city above the ground, built within trees” he whispered not able to comprehend what he was seeing. The architecture was some of the most beautiful he had ever seen, and he drank it in as the mid day sun highlighted the gleaming silver accents over the dark wooden beams and lattice over the outside of the structures. “I see you are awake” came a new voice from behind and Marcus turned and nearly fell as he came face to face with someone who was not quite human. His eyes were too big, his lanky frame and green hued skin were a contrast to Marcus’s own. Extending his hand Marcus extended his own, past the man’s two long three fingers and grasping his wrist greeted the newcomer.

The man smiled; his white uniform resplendent with metals that were unrecognizable to Marcus “I see you have never met a Sylvan” he remarked good naturedly. Marcus nodded his head “You sir, would be my first” he said regaining his composure. The man smiled good naturedly “I am General Durass, would you have a few moments to speak with me?” he asked, and Marcus appreciated the man making it a request, as far as he could tell they were at his mercy. “Of course, General” Marcus said and followed the man as they entered a private office. Marcus entered the Generals’ private sanctum looking at the dark wood sculptures used to support the walls and the lines and lines of shelves that held the handwritten copies of books. The room made him feel at home and relaxed in some primal way.

The General motioned for Marcus to take a chair and walked around the large mahogany desk to sit across from him. Sitting there he regarded the man looking him over silently. Marcus stared back, neither man saying a word as they sized each other up. Finally, the General broke the silence. “So, it seems everyone wants you Marcus Gavin, though a mage but not of the order and rumored to be quite powerful if our spies are worth their salt. Between the Empress and the neighboring countries, they have expended a lot of resources in tracking you down, why is that I wonder?” he finished his eyes never wavering from Marcus’s.

“Im a popular guy” Marcus said flatly carefully watching the General, will he turn me over, or could these people want me as well he wondered looking for intent in the Generals words, movements or eyes. To his benefit General Durass smiled giving off a light chuckle as he shook his head. “You have nothing to fear Marcus Gavin, while we understand and embrace magic, we have no lust for power as do your people” he said nailing Marcus’s worry on the head. The General shifted uncomfortably in his seat as he turned his head to stare out a window on the far wall. “I have to ask you something, bear with me please, your friends told us your story, is it true you fell from the sky?” he asked turning to look at Marcus again except this time there was a light in the General’s eyes one that Marcus couldn’t place. He simply nodded and the other man smiled. “Where were you?” he asked the question was simple, yet there was no simple answer Marcus could think of finally he settled for the truth. “The ones you call the ancients, tried to save our way of life, taking many of us they sent us into the sky to sleep for centuries, looks like I was late coming back” Marcus said and proffered the man a weak smile. The General cocked his head and squinted at him. “Are you sure about that?” he asked and giving him a questioning look Marcus motioned for his to continue, what was he trying to get at the young mage wondered. “I mean, maybe you weren’t late, maybe you are exactly where you are supposed to be” he said and then made a holding motion as Marcus began to speak, to argue.

“My people have a legend of the sions, those who fell to earth there was one who was destined to fall only when he was needed, until then he slept in the sky until summoned, I wonder Marcus Gavin, might you have landed right when you need to” the General Proffered arching an eyebrow slyly. Marcus smiled “General, I am no legend, just a man who was late to the party” he said simply not really knowing how to respond to him. General Durass simply shrugged. “Anyway, you might notice that our people stare a bit, for that I apologize apparently the Warden to found you inadvertently told the Soldiers what she knew of your story and your mage friends filled in the rest, word has gotten around” he finished and Marcus sighed.

The last thing he needed was hero worship, hell he didn’t know what he needed he thought, he was a man lost, his mentor and friend and the love of his life were both dead, he had just run from a country that had relentlessly hunted him and enslaved its people and now, now he was here and this man had just told him he was some sort of legend. With a sign Marcus lowered his head and closed his eyes, he was tired so very tired, and he was a man without a purpose or a cause, a man who felt far older than his twenty-five years. He sat there with is eyes closed remember lost friends and family for what seemed like an eternity. Finally, the General spoke, his tone gentle as he broke through Marcus’s Malaise. “You think you are lost Marcus, but you have a purpose, you have a gift and there are those that need you, implore you to become the protector you were meant to be. I noticed the marking on your arm, what does it say?” he asked and Marcus opened his eyes to see the cross pistols and banner that flew underneath it tattooed on his arm.

Remnants of a drunken night with fellow graduates of the United States Army Military Police School and smiled “It says General, This well defend” he finished the words coming from his mouth and resounding in his head. He did have a gift, he still had a purpose, these might not be his people but they were people, innocent people who now faced a threat of a Empress who hunted him relentlessly, a Empress who’s underlings killed his love and who’s chosen had killed his friend” he thought.

He could try and fool himself tell himself that it was duty that pulled him from his funk, but no, Marcus knew better it was vengeance. He needed to see those who had taken his friend and lover away from him, who had not given him a moments peace since landing. He needed to stop the Empress he finally thought putting into a direct thought something that had played at his mind over and over, whispered in the dark corners of his mind as he passed the travesties of villages and now even moreso after Rogan’s execution of his friend and mentor. But he had fought Rogan, had seen the power the Seer had wielded, how could he combat that he wondered. But he had four generations of knowledge he thought, but how to access it his troubled thoughts must have crossed his face because the General sat forward.

“Whats wrong Marcus?” he asked looking concerned. He explained the fight with the Lord Seer “General, I am powerful, I get that, I have knowledge I can’t access yet that could help if I could figure it out. But this Seer his power was well beyond me, I saw it manifest through the runes carved into his skin, watched as it doubled and grew far beyond my own ability, from what I understand that should not be possible” Marcus finished and the General nodded looking away and then back to Marcus. “You saw the power, watched as it manifested through the Runes?” he asked again he had that odd look on his face that Marcus couldn’t place. He nodded to him and the man shook his head astounded. “You are a Rune Wright Marcus, but its more then that, you have a relationship with the Magic that is rare, but not unheard of, you can follow the path of the magic, understand its flavor, which might not make sense right now, but one day, it will” he continued sitting back in the large chair

“As for the runes it’s a skill called Hitrashi, its something our people perfected generations ago allowing us to maintain our mage abilities in those that manifested them, I have no idea how the Empress learned this though, this is disturbing. Marcus if they have scribed the Seer’s then they are indeed powerful mages and nothing on this world can stand against them save you and maybe a handful of our own Master Magi” he finished looking into the distance, as if lost in his thoughts. “I need you to meet someone, someone who might be able to help, if you agree” he said, not getting up, waiting for Marcus to either agree or decline.

He thought about it for only a moment if the Silvan’s did indeed have someone who might be able to help him access the knowledge in his mind, that could be valuable, a Master had died giving it to him, did he really want to simply waste that sacrifice he thought. Coming to his feet he decided and nodded his head “Lets go” he said Durass smiled, guiding Marcus out of the room and instead of heading to the front door, they descended into the lower levels of the house. Walking to the far corner of the basement, if that was what you could call it, Durass moved a statue and the bookcase that took up most of the wall slid away, revealing a dark passage.

He picked up a crystal lantern and beckoned Marcus to follow. Marcus did, walking into the tunnel that looked as if it where hollowed out of a large branch, one big enough for him to walk standing upright. They continued for only a short time before coming to a spiral staircase, the entire tunnel and stairs carved out of wood. “Where are we?” Marcus asked looking around Durass followed his eyes and then smiled, as if enjoying Marcus’s confusion. “We are inside a tree, you see like your Order of the Dragon, our mages are mystics but hidden from the populace no one knows who they are only that they exist and aid our people” he finished stopping for a moment and pulling up the sleeve of his shirt to reveal what looked like a Phoenix burned into his forearm. “So, you are a member” Marcus asked some of his comments making more sense.

“I am, but the one I take you to meet is my master, he is very Old Marcus, older then you can imagine and his knowledge may help you, and in helping you it could help my people” he began, his shoulders slumping as he continued to descend the stairs. “You see, the Empress is gathering her army, the soldiers on the border are still there, but Warden’s keep is swelling with six of her twelve Seer’s as well as three battalions of soldiers, she means to March on the Barrens, though for what reason I don’t know why, we have never threatened her. But she is determined to conquer ever corner of the territories and beyond” he said and though the crystal lamp light he could see the worry in the general’s large eyes. Marcus now understood why the General would want to help him. In helping him he would help his people. Marcus could appreciate this and suddenly felt better as if knowing the other man’s motivations made him more trustworthy.

They came to the bottom of the spiral stairs after what seemed an eternity and then began to walk down a larger tunnel, but this one was stone. “We are underground” Marcus said and Durass smiled of course. The stone looked ancient, covered with old moss as water trickled down and the sound of dripping echoed throughout the long dark tunnel.

Finally, it opened up into a large Cavern and Marcus gaped, it appeared as if they were inside a giant green crystal, every surface was glassy, smooth and green. “This is amazing” he breathed not knowing a word that could justify what he was seeing. General Durass looked up smiling “It took us generations to grow and carve, it is the source of power for our Mages, the place they go to complete the rituals needed to transform one into a Korlestor” he said and Marcus shot him a questioning gaze Durass shrugged, roughly translated it means ghost walker” he said, it is one who has been marked with the runes unlocking there true potential of power.

But it can only, truly be done by one who can see the magic and shape the runes to that Mage, you see the Empress might have learned the art, but when you watched the magic coalesce through the seer, how did it look” Durass asked and Marcus thought about it, closing his eyes and remembering watching the magic began to flow through the runes. “It was dark in areas, bleeding power in others, it looked... inefficient” he finally said putting a word to what he had seen. Durass nodded as if knew “She followed whatever guide she managed to get ahold of, but she didn’t understand it, the color of the runes told me that” he finished, and they continued making their way across the cavernous crystal cavern. As they walked a booming voice echoed over the entire cavern.

“Who is brought before me” came a booming voice and Marcus could see the power as it emanated from the walls itself, someone was using power to amplify their voice he realized looking around. Durass stood there and straightened his back. “I bring one with the power, one with the sight who wishes to unlock his true potential” he stated as if this were some ritual that needed to play out. Marcus stayed quiet watching and waiting as the booming voice returned. “Send the one forward, he and he alone must approach to start his journey” the booming voice said. “If he has the sight, he will know the way” it concluded and it was right, Marcus could see a pulsing twisting line of power as it wove its way across the floor and into the darkness.

“Go ahead, I will come find you when you are done” Durass whispered and then put a gentle hand on his shoulder. “Good Luck Marcus” he simply said and then he was gone, walking back the way they had come.

Marcus saw the line, flowing forward into the distance and began to follow it, keeping to the line as best he could he walked into the darkness, it was unsettling not knowing how far the wall was or if there was even a floor, it was as if the only things that existed where himself and the line of power. Marcus followed the line for close to thirty minutes, walking forward with his hands out but nothing obstructed his approach and then the line simply stopped, So Marcus stopped with it. “What is your name child?” came an ancient and raspy voice from in front of him.

“I, I am Marcus Gavin” he said and waited. “Show me your power Marcus Gavin” the voice rasped and for a moment he didn’t understand but then he thought he did. Summoning power he created a small sphere of fire holding it above his hand he continued to feed power into it, watching as it grew brighter and hotter, finally he had to squint his eyes, he kept feeding it for a time, until he felt his energy ebb and released his will, the fire disappearing. Marcus waited in the silence that follow, feeling as if the old voice was making some sort of judgement.

“Marcus Gavin, you wield the power of those of the first, we have the power to unlock your potential, we have the power to unlock your knowledge, but we have a fear” the voice said

“What fear do you have?” he asked wondering where this was going. “You have lost Marcus, we feel the anger in your soul, we know much has been taken from you, but darkness has a way of taking over and the gifts we offer would make you a powerful enemy of the land, can you understand our hesitation” he said and after a moment continued. “What motivates you Marcus, tell us what drives that which is you” the voice said, and Marcus took a mental step back. What kind of question was that he thought, how the hell was he supposed to answer it? He thought about if a moment and then an answer came to him, from somewhere deep within the words bubbled forth. “You are correct, I am angry for my loss, but that is not what drives me. I am a warrior, a protector one who served to protect those who could not protect themselves. A defender of a way of living I believed was just. I do have hate and I do want vengeance, but these are not my core motivations” He said and again there was a silence This well defend he thought and smiled remembering the motto of the Army Military Police.

“Your words speak true Marcus Gavin, approach so that we may be known to you” the voice said and a light emanated from somewhere, in the center of it was a very old Silvan, his dark hair had gone white and his overly large eyes were milky with cataracts he stood there hunched over a small wooden cane. “Approach my child” the old man said, and Marcus slowly walked forward, not sure what to make of this person. He was obviously old and probably damn near blind he thought.

The old man stood in front of him, nearly half Marcus’s size he regarded him with those old milky eyes “I am Borr, Master Mage of the Phoenix, you are Marcus Gavin, of the old Power, well met my child” the old man rasped smiling up at him, his gums white with age and free of any teeth. “It is good to meet you” Marcus intoned curious as to wether the old man could actually see him. After a moment the ancient and decrepit man turned and with a motion walked further into the room, the light seeming to follow him. Marcus did as well. As they reached the center of the large area the light spread showing the rest of the cavernous chamber, he now found himself in. Green crystal walls shone back at him, so clear he could see his reflection as if in a mirror he thought. Was the room big he really wondered or was it merely a trick. But he couldn’t follow that thought the old Mage gesturing him to a chair that he was sure, hadn’t been there a moment ago.

Marcus sat as the old man also took a seat in one across from him. Okay he thought that definitely wasn’t there a moment ago. “You fought one of the Empress’s Seers, you have seen the power they wield” it wasn’t a question, it was a statement as if this old man already knew that. “Yes” Marcus said anyway as if needing to provide an answer despite the tone of the not question. He nodded “The Empress dabbles in knowledge she doesn’t understand, theories she only barely comprehends but does so in order to provide herself the ability to control those around her. Almost like a monkey learning to use a gun, it might figure out how to pull a trigger and where to point it, but it doesn’t understand the theory or that sooner or later it will run out of ammunition” the old man stated, but Marcus thought it was more to himself then to him.

Then the old man was standing next to Marcus causing him to jump. He hadn’t seen him move, he was suddenly just there and then he placed old, cold fingers on his skull and the Milky white eyes fluttered as he stood there gently prodding Marcsus’s skull. “Its true, you do have the knowledge, but it is not accessible to you yet, given time it will manifest itself allowing you access to portions of it, finally unlocking over time. But I would guess you have a need for it now” the old man said smiling as he stood next to him.

“I believe it might help” He answered the old man and he did, the three generations of knowledge of magic, weapons, fighting and history could be very useful right now, he didn’t have time to wait a decade or so for it to finally become available. The old man nodded, shuffling away from Marcus “We will get to that, first we need to work on you” he said and motioned for Marcus to stand. “The low landers have a rudimentary knowledge of how the relationship between the magic and the runes work, thus the clumsy focus run you now wear on your hand” he said pointing to Marcus’s leather glove.

“You see, the runes help gather, store and dispense power, it allows you to weave the energy, collecting more and folding it into itself making the power you have gathered greater, more concentrated and then allowing your mind to focus it to a pinpoint if you choose. But it’s not something that is generic, not a pattern you can apply. It is specific to the mage based on there power and their flavor of magic” the old man said seeming to study Marcus.

“I don’t know, I saw and felt the power that Seer wielded, it was massive” Marcus said wincing at the memory of breaking bones. The old mage nodded “As it would seem to one who has no knowledge of such things” he stated matter of factly and for a moment Marcus tried to figure out if that was just a statement or had he insulted him. Before he could run that down in his mind, he felt a force take hold of him, taking the breath from his body as a glowly representation of his body emerged from within himself, coming to float between himself and the old man.

Marcus stared at it trying to understand what he was seeing. As if the old man understood the thoughts in his head he nodded “This is a magical representation of you, or more to the point your power” he said and then reached out with the end of his cane and drew a sigil on Marcus’s phantom chest. It pulsed and glowed with power, but a corner of it was dim as if the power wasn’t flowing to that curve of the sigil. Tentivaly reaching out he took the tip of his finger, tracing the curve and moving it slightly making it a little wider at the same time. It took three tries but finally as he pulled his finger away, the sigil pulsed uniformly, and the old mage nodded in approval.

“Low Landers believe that Runes are general, and they do work, but the same way a starving horse can still run, just not as fast as a well fed one” the old man smiled amused at his own analogy. “Runes are a template, but they need to be worked to match the power of the Mage using them or they will never reach their full potential” he finished drawing a second run that intersected the first one with a connector of sorts. Marcus again saw where it didn’t quite flow and fixed it, they continued to do this for the next six hours, the old mage drawing on the phantom simulacrum of Marcus and then the younger Mage fixing it, make it fit the power that pulsed through it.

When they had finished Marcus walked around the floating semi-transparent body looking as the entirety of it was covered with runes, except for the hands and beyond the neck, on the hands a line ran out connecting to what looked like a stylized eye on each palm. Marcus could see what the old mage meant, the power was uniform, clean and pulsing. The runes on the Seer, with his sight still seemed dimmed and dark in places, the power never fully being utilized.

“Okay, what do we do now” Marcus asked excitedly, and the old Mage chuckled “Now young Mage, we eat” he said and waved his hand, a dozen feat from them a table was there, just instantly there and covered with food. Marcus realizing, he was ravenous. The two walked over each taking a seat across from one another and began loading plates.

“This is all a lot to take in” he said shaking his head as he ate. The old Mage chuckled “Do you believe in destiny Marcus Gavin?” he asked and marcus thought about it “No, I don’t think there is some plan for everyone, I think life is just a series of random choices and events” he finished and again the old Mage simply chuckled. “For a man who slept for centuries, well past his own people, landed at a time when the world was breaking, met an old Mage who gave him not only his knowledge but the knowledge of the last three masters before him and now stand someplace a lowlander hasn’t stood since the time of the first ones, yet, you still think its all random” the mage asked teasingly.

Marcus thought about it for a moment “Okay, lets say you’re right, whats the reason then?” he asked honestly wanting to know, if there was a plan, surely someone knew what that plan was. But the old man shook his head “I don’t know for sure young Mage, but I can guess” he began, and Marcus motioned for him to continue as he refilled his place with a steaming pile of spicy meat.

“The Empress has taken knowledge not her own and preferred it to use against those who can’t defend themselves against it, she has broken faith and taken the magic of our people to use as a weapon to gain control of everything, you have the ability to balance that Marcus, you have the ability to stand against her and heal the world” the old Mage said, his words ringing with truth, Marcus had not seen it like that and thought about his time here, the events that have transpired and led him to this place, this time.

Was it possible he thought, was there something guiding the events to bring him to a place where he could defend the land against someone who so obviously was power mad, no he thought that’s a little too far down the rabbit hole? The old man seemed to sense his thoughts and chuckled “Fortunately destiny does not require believe” he simply said and continued eating.

After they ate Marcus realized he wasn’t tired, in fact he felt revitalized “How am I not tired?” he asked “I am still healing and we have been working for nearly twelve hours” he said and the old mage smiled “We are inside a giant crystal, it feeds us power, its what keeps me alive and re-energizes us, we don’t need sleep here my friend” he finished. “Can you leave the crystal?” Marcus asked gently thinking he already knew the answer. “Alas, I cannot I have lived well beyond the years my body could possibly function on its own, without the power of the crystal I would simply die, my organs failing as they should have at least a century ago” he said sadly. Marcus thought about it, realizing it wasn’t a gift, it was a prison to live without the ability to live. “Why do you do it?” he asked wondering why someone who torture themselves like that” he simply smiled wanly at the young Mage “because I am needed” he answered simply.

“I was the one who grew the trees so large we could build a city in them, I created beasts of burden for our people that served them better then the horses of the lowlands and much more” he said and Marcus wondered what he was talking about “you created animals?” he asked and the old Mage merely smiled, walking back over to the pulsing simulacrum. “Now Marcus we need to make the polymer resin that will allow us to bond this to your body, are you ready?” he asked, and Marcus nodded the excitement of learning gleaming in his eyes. With a wave of his hand a table appeared, littered with bottles of power, liquids mortar and pestles and small bottles over fire. “What is this?” he asked curiously looking over the table as they both approached it.

“Here we will build a compound that will be tough but flexible, made of the crystal compounds, resin and some metals that will allow you to conduct power through the runic sigil we have created for you.” He finished and began to add sprinkles of various crystal dust, metal and other components into a central bowl that stood over a blue flame. He talked Marcus through each compound, explaining its properties and its measurements, teaching marcus the means to create a runic mage he realized the term coming from somewhere in his mind.

“What is a runic mage?” he asked and with a start the old mage looked up at him. “It’s the lowlander word for our ghost walker, it’s the culmination of a battletrained mage with runic enhancements, basically it is the culmination of years of training, learning and the introduction of the mages rune” he finished and the nodded with approval. “It seems that the knowledge is slowly becoming available already Marcus”. They worked through the night and well into the next day, each step taking an exact time of production, creation and cooking before the next step could be started. Finally, the old Mage added the final ingredient and as Marcus watched the black compound turned bright blue as it pulsed with an energy of its own. “But the Seers sigils were black” he said making a question out of the statement. The old Mage smiled showing his gums as he chuckled “The Empress has basic knowledge, but she doesn’t understand the concepts, when creating the mixture she did not understand timing and lacked the final ingredient, the resin works, but breaks down after a few years and is inefficient in conduction” the Ancient Mage said.

His face then turned serious “Undress” he said, and Marcus looked at him curiously, but the old mage simply stood there waiting. Marcus slowly undressed, the mage motioning him to remove the bandages as well. Finally, Marcus was on display completely naked, he surprisingly enough found that his bruises were gone, and his bones were fully healed. “Being inside a power crystal has interesting benefits” the old man said smiling again. “It’s the reason we do this here, anywhere else would almost surely be deadly” he said and then with a wave of his hand the polymer began to stream out of the bowl and hang in the air.

As Marcus watched it began to mimic and match the sigil they had created, making an exact copy of it, as it hung there next to the phantom simulacrum. “Pour power into it Marcus, we need to make sure its ready before we apply it” the old Mage said and Marcus gathered a small amount of energy, pushing it into the body length sigil and watched as it pulsed with power. They both carefully studied it, Marcus pushing power at it four more times until the old mage was satisfied. Finally his smile faded and he turned to look at the young mage “I apologize for this” he said and Marcus was about to ask what he was talking about when the sigil simply flew at him, slamming into his body as it flowed over his skin, covering him completely, but it didn’t stop, it began to move and flow faster as he felt it bite into every inch of his skin. Marcus screamed as pain erupted over his entire body as the compound sliced into his skin, digging down past the epidermis to rest against muscle, slicing up and then bonding with his skin.

Marcus passed out, the world mercifully going dark as his body pushed well past its pain threshold shut down to protect itself.

After a time, he woke, his body no longer hurting, picking himself off of the floor he saw his naked arms and legs. They glowed blue the compound not covering his skin, but replacing it, merging to become a part of him, not merely a decoration. “What the” he said standing and staring at the crystal wall, his entire body a winding glowing pattern. But more then that, he felt power flowing through the sigil like a river running over his body. The power he felt was incredible as he finally began to understand the power he could wield. “Congratulations Marcus Gavin, as your people say you are the First Runic Mage in a generation” he stated, standing back and admiring the young man. Marcus finally began to feel a little self conscious as it dawned on him, he was still completely naked. Putting on the leather mages outfit he shrugged his shoulders as if the outfit wasn’t comfortable. But it wasn’t the outfit, it was the feeling of power coursing through the runes. “Don’t worry, give it time and you will get used to it, it will constantly flow with power as a part of you and your power, it connects the energy of the world to your will in a way using the crystals to gather energy never did” he finished and Marcus cocked his head at him.

“Do you mean, we don’t gather energy from the crystals?” he asked and the Old Mage smiled “No, mages do require crystals in order to gather power, but the crystal gathers power from its environment for the mage to draw on, now you and the crystal are one Marcus, you can merely draw energy from around you, every atomic is power, you can now draw upon the universe to power your magic” he finished. Marcus simply shook his head, he didn’t even begin to comprehend the theory, it would take him a century of study to truly understand the meaning of that statement he thought.

“Now, you will need access to your knowledge If you are to create the tools you need for the coming war child” the old Mage said almost sadly and with that he snapped his fingers, Marcus gasped as his eyes went black for a moment, like a curtain being lifted he suddenly had access to everything, understood, everything.

Knew the theories of Magic, power, the universe how power was given to the mages and more importantly he understood combat, tactics, spells and how to construct the weapons and armor he would need. More importantly he knew had a level of knowledge since he had the ability to see the flow of power. “That is, incredible” he gasped looking at the old man. He shambled over to Marcus “I have one more gift child, my people have maintained a balance between magic and technology yours have not, so my gift to you is technology and innovation” he said and slammed his old wrinkled hand on Marcus’s head and like a damn bursting knowledge flew into his head matching with the understand of weapons, armor and devices as if they had never truly been complete, when he was done the old man took his hand away, though now it shook noticeably.

“I need to go rest, but you my child, need to create the war is coming and you need to be ready” he said and pointed, as Marcus followed his hand he saw a area of the cavern now help a smithing area, smelting area, crafting tables with specialized tools and stacks and stacks of materials. “Its time to build the things you will need” he said and then turned to go. “Wait, will I see you again?” Marcus asked feeling a sadness that he might now.

The old mage smiled “I think you might young one, I just think you might” he finished and with that the light around him dimmed and he was gone. Turning back to the area he looked over the tables and machines nodding his head. He did have a lot to do and he might not have a lot of time to complete it he thought.
